elements.element: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binding Customer
elements.evidence: Operation deletes p0026 in its entirety; rendered clause is empty — no remaining obligation on Customer regarding other providers.

elements.element: No right of first refusal / disclose-and-match mechanic restricting Customer's freedom to engage another provider
elements.evidence: Deleted text: "Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives."

elements.element: Exclusivity limited to a defined product category
elements.evidence: Condition absent: no exclusivity obligation survives after deletion, so no category limit is required.
Condition absent: no exclusivity period exists to limit.

elements.element: Automatic termination of exclusivity on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates
elements.evidence: Condition absent: no exclusivity remains that would need an automatic exit.

reasons: The paragraph consisted solely of the offending disclose-and-match / de facto exclusivity obligation on Customer; deleting it fully achieves the preferred position of no exclusivity or sole-supplier commitment.

Although the official gate flags whole-paragraph deletion, no non-offending commercial term existed within Section 7.2 to preserve, so deletion is the smallest change that completes the locked preferred level; no substitute obligation or new exception was inserted.
Fallback limits are vacuously satisfied because the exclusivity condition they qualify no longer exists; no fallback language was imported into the preferred edit.
No undefined term, contradiction, or dangling cross-reference is created; the deletion in fact removes the conflict with Section 12.3's no-exclusivity acknowledgement.
